δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι, 
 [in LXX for בָּרַח hi., Exo.26:28 * ;] 
to go through, penetrate: Heb.4:12.†
 (AS)

ἐθελο-θρησκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ, 
 self-imposed worship: Col.2:23 (eccl.; cf. DB, iv, 923a; Cremer, 733).†
 (AS)

Ἑλληνικκός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX: Jer.46:6 50:16 (יָנָה: aliter in Heb.), 2Ma.4:10 2Mac 4:15 2Mac 6:9 2Mac 11:24 2Mac 13:2, 4Ma.8:8 * ;] 
Greek: τ. Ἑλληνικῇ (sc. γλωσσῇ), Rev.9:11.†
 (AS)

ἐμ-παιγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
 (ἐμπαίζω, which see), [in LXX: Eze.22:4 (קַלָּסָה), Ps 38:7 B א1 קָלָה ni.), Wis.12:2, Sir.27:28, 2Ma.7:7, 3Ma.5:22 * ;] 
a mocking: Heb.11:36.†
 (AS)

ἑρμηνεύω 
 [in LXX: Est.4:7 (תִּרְגַּם), Est.10:3 Job.42:17β* ;] 
__1. to explain. 
 __2. to interpret: Luk.24:27 (WH, mg.), Jhn.1:39, 43 9:7, Heb.7:2.† 
 (AS)

εὐ-φορέω, -ῶ 
 to be fruitful: Luk.12:16.†
 (AS)

εὐφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
 (εὔφρων, cheerful) [in LXX chiefly for שִׂמְחָה ;] 
rejoicing, gladness: Act.2:28 (LXX) Act.14:17.†
 (AS)

κατα-παύω 
 [in LXX for נוּחַ, שָׁבַת, etc. ;] 
__1. trans., 
 __(a) to cause to cease, restrain: Act.14:18; 
 __(b) to cause to rest: Heb.4:8. 
 __2. Intrans., to rest: before ἀτό, Heb.4:4 (LXX), Heb.4:10.†
 (AS)

κενοφωνία, -ας, ἡ
 (κενός, φωνέω), [cf. κενολογέω (צָפַף), Isa.8:19 * ;] 
empty talk, babbling: pl., 1Ti.6:20, 2Ti.2:16.†
 (AS)

κοπιάω, -ῶ
 (κόπος), [in LXX chiefly for יָגַע ;] 
__1. (as in cl.) to grow weary: Mat.11:28, Jhn.4:6, Rev.2:3 (cf. Isa.40:31). 
 __2. Hence, in LXX and NT, to work with effort, to toil: absol., Mat.6:23, Luk.5:5 12:27, Jhn.4:38, Act.20:35, 1Co.4:12, Eph.4:28, 2Ti.2:5; with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.4:38; frequently in Paul. Epp., of ministerial labour: 1Co.15:10 16:16; before ἐν, Rom.16:12, 1Th.5:12 (see M, Th., in l), 1Ti.5:17; εἰς, Rom.16:6, Gal.4:11, Php.2:16, Col.1:29, 1Ti.4:10.†
 (AS)

λεγιών (Rec. -εών), -ῶνος, ἡ, (Lat. legio), 
 a legion: Mat.26:53, Mrk.5:9, 15, Luk.8:30.†
 (AS)

λύστρα, -ας, ἡ 
 and (in Act.14:8 16:2, 2Ti, l.with) -ων, τά (cf. Λύδδα), 
 Lystra, a city of Lycaonia: Act.14:6, 8 14:21 16:1-2, 2Ti.3:11.†
 (AS)

Ὀλυμπᾶς
 (perh. contr. fr. Ὀλνμπιόδωρος, Bl., § 29), -ᾶ, 
Olympas: Rom.16:15.†
 (AS)

πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό
 (cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand), 
pre-judging, prejudice: 1Ti.5:21 (see Cremer, 378).†
 (AS)

σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;] 
fine wheaten flour: Rev.18:13.†
 (AS)

συν-κύπτω
 (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.9:27 (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 19:26 * ;] 
__1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.). 
 __2. to be bowed down: Luk.13:11.†
 (AS)

Ἀντιοχεύς, -έως, ὁ 
 a citizen of Antioch, an Antiochian: Act.6:5.†
 (AS)

σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό 
 (σῆμα), [in LXX: Jdg.20:38, 40 (מַשְׂאֵת), Isa.5:26 49:22 62:10 (נֵס) * ;] 
a fixed sign or signal: Mrk.14:44. (Strab., Plut., al.; condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 492 f.) †
 (AS)

Ἄβελ, (WH, Ἅ-), ὁ, indecl. 
 (הֶבֶל), 
Abel (Gen.4:2-10): Heb.11:4, 12:24; αἵμα Ἄ., Mat.23:35, Luk.11:51.† 
 (AS)

ἀπο-κλείω 
 [in LXX chiefly for סָגַר ;] 
to shut fast: Luk.13:25.†
 (AS)

ἅρμα, -τος, τό
 (ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רָכַב ;] 
a chariot: Act.8:28-29, 38, Rev.9:9.†
 (AS)

ἀ-χρεῖος, -ον
 (χρεῖος, useful), [in LXX: 2Ki.6:22 (שָׁפָל), Ep. Jer.17:1-27 * ;] 
useless, unprofitable: Mat.25:30, Luk.17:10 (MM, see word).†
 (AS)

Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, see Westc. on Jhn.5:2, and DB, i, 279), 
 Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jhn.5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).†
 (AS)

§ Galilee = "circuit, district"
 a territory in Naphtali largely occupied by heathen; a circuit of towns around Kedesh-Naphtali, in which were situated the 20 towns given by Solomon to Hiram king of Tyre as payment for his work in conveying timber from Lebanon to Jerusalem

A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at 2Ch.17.8
 § Jehoram or Joram = "Jehovah is exalted"
1) son of king Jehoshaphat of Judah and himself king of Judah for 8 years; his wife was the wicked Athaliah who was probably the instigator for his returning the nation of Judah to the worship of Baal
2) son of king Ahab of the northern kingdom of Israel and king of Israel himself for 12 years; he was murdered by Jehu on the plot of land for which his father had murdered Naboth thus fulfilling the prophecy of Elijah to the very letter
3) a priest in the reign of Jehoshaphat
